convergence_checkpoints.checkpoint: commit_legacy_capture (the ordinary v1 delegate HistoricalStudyVerifier.capture calls per Decision point 8(d)) and inspect_capture_admission's reused _validate_capture_request both read the SAME broker._p4_ledger._legacy_captures()/_nonces state -- a LITERAL repeat capture() call reusing the identical (published, frozen, port) a first, successful capture already consumed refuses at inspect_capture_admission's own F4-stream-liveness/nonce-freshness check, BEFORE ever reaching reserve_once's own (False, seq) 'consumed admission is spent' path. This is real, not a construction mistake: after the FIRST successful capture(), the stream is durably CAPTURED at the F4 level (a pre-existing, unrelated one-way transition this ADR does not touch), and _validate_capture_request (reused, per Decision point 3b, unchanged) refuses ANY further request referencing that same stream -- independent of admission_ref, nonce freshness, or the ledger's own state.
convergence_checkpoints.resolution: not an architecture contradiction requiring a design change: the SAFETY property Decision point 8/11 actually demands (no second admission_use record; authority.capture never invoked a second time for the same admission) holds in EITHER case -- verified directly in the RED/GREEN tests. Row 2's/row 6's 'literal same-stream repeat' tests now assert the real, observable safety invariants (bind pytest.raises(ValueError) generically, plus 'no second record / audit unchanged') with a comment explaining which check fires and why. A SEPARATE, deterministic test (test_ledger_already_spent_refusal_is_isolated_from_f4_stream_state, plus test_a_fresh_unused_nonce_still_collides_on_the_same_admission_key for row 10) isolates reserve_once's own exact 'CAPTURED refuses after consumed admission is spent' message by pre-seeding the SAME reservation a concurrent thread or a crashed prior attempt would leave (i.e. BEFORE authority.capture ever touches the F4 stream), proving that path is genuinely reachable and correct on its own terms. Disclosed here in full per the convergence-checkpoint pattern rather than silently rewording the matrix's own expected_outcome text.

convergence_checkpoints.checkpoint: JsonlLedger._open()'s existing recovery walk (unchanged by this ADR) rebuilds only self._seq/_head/_index/snapshot-cadence from disk; it never calls self._state.apply(envelope) during recovery -- SeriesState.apply is only ever invoked, going forward, by future _commit calls. Decision point 10's 'replays the entire verified chain from genesis... via JsonlLedger._open's own existing recovery walk... followed by one state.apply(envelope) call per record' therefore cannot be satisfied by ChainLedger.__init__ alone; it is HistoricalStudyVerifier.durable(...)'s own responsibility, layered on top of the generic ChainLedger open.
convergence_checkpoints.resolution: not a contradiction -- ChainLedger stays a generic base (Non-goals: 'no change to JsonlLedger's five store hooks'); durable()'s own body performs the explicit replay (for envelope in ledger.scan(): state.apply(envelope)) immediately after construction and refuses (ProductionError, closing the ledger) if the replayed SeriesState's own head disagrees with the ledger's independently verified head, exactly as Decision point 10 specifies. Documented in verifier.py's own comment at the call site.
